mission.title: Install and Configure Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)
mission.description: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the process of running Kubernetes on AWS. It provides a highly available and scalable Kubernetes control plane, making it ideal for production workloads. Key trade-offs include reliance on AWS infrastructure and potential costs associated with managed services.

steps.title: Install the AWS CLI
steps.description:
The AWS CLI is required to interact with AWS services, including EKS. Ensure you have the latest version installed.

```bash

pip install awscli --upgrade --user

```

> Install or upgrade AWS CLI to the latest version.

steps.title: Create an EKS Cluster
steps.description:
This command creates an EKS cluster with the specified Kubernetes version and node count in a given region.

```bash

aws eks create-cluster --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.31 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID:role/EKS-Cluster-Role --resources-vpc-config subnetIds=subnet-12345678,subnet-87654321,securityGroupIds=sg-12345678 --region us-west-2

```

> Replace YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID with your actual AWS account ID.

steps.title: Update kubeconfig
steps.description:
This command updates your kubeconfig file to use the new EKS cluster, allowing you to interact with it using kubectl.

```bash

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name my-cluster --region us-west-2

```

> Ensure you are using the correct region.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in your EKS cluster to ensure they are running correctly.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes listed with a status of 'Ready'.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
Set up necessary configurations such as autoscaling and monitoring for your EKS cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/master/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/examples/cluster-autoscaler.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/metrics-server/master/deploy/1.8+/metrics-server-deployment.yaml

```

> This sets up the cluster autoscaler.
> This installs the metrics server for monitoring.

uninstall.title: Delete the EKS Cluster
uninstall.description:
This command deletes the EKS cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss and orphaned resources.

```bash

aws eks delete-cluster --name my-cluster --region us-west-2

aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id sg-12345678

```

> Delete any associated security groups if not needed.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the EKS Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your workloads and configurations. This command upgrades the cluster to a new Kubernetes version.

```bash

aws eks update-cluster-version --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.31 --region us-west-2

kubectl get nodes

```

> Monitor the upgrade process for any issues.
> Verify that all nodes are in 'Ready' state after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This usually indicates a problem with the kubeconfig file or permissions.

**Fix:**
Run 'aws eks update-kubeconfig --name my-cluster --region us-west-2' to refresh the kubeconfig.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'No resources found in kube-system namespace'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the cluster is not fully initialized or if the necessary components are not deployed.

**Fix:**
Check the status of the cluster with 'aws eks describe-cluster --name my-cluster --region us-west-2'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient permissions to perform this operation'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The IAM role associated with your AWS CLI user may not have the necessary permissions.

**Fix:**
Ensure your IAM role has the required permissions for EKS operations.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create cluster: VPC already exists'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the specified VPC or subnets are already in use.

**Fix:**
Choose a different VPC or delete the existing resources before retrying.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for Kubernetes 1.31, improved integration with AWS services.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated support for Kubernetes versions below 1.28.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: Ensure your workloads are compatible with the new version before upgrading.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' showing the nodes in 'Ready' state, confirming that the EKS cluster is operational.

prerequisites.description: Ensure you have the necessary tools and resources before starting the installation.
